title.narrative: UNICEF Child Protection and WASH System strengthening in Sudan
UNICEF Child Protection and WASH System strengthening in Sudan

description.narrative:
For the proposed programme, UNICEF will work on strengthening social welfare and justice systems at state and local levels in relatively stable states to ensure the delivery of integrated and specialized child protection services and basic sustainable water, sanitation, and hygiene services. It is Sidas assessment that this is in-line with Sidas focus on strenghtening long-term development in Sudan.
Objectives will be achieved through support to the social service workforce and frontline workers in the host communities receiving high number of displaced people and through effective community mobilisation with a focus on sustainable services.
Expected impact/results
WASH service provision will be enhanced in vulnerable communities, ensuring integration with child protection, education, and health and nutrition sectors. This will be delivered through a mix of interventions including the rehabilitation or construction of water and sanitation infrastructure in communities, child friendly spaces and health centres.
Activities will include social mobilization to stop open defecation in the communities, and the promotion of hygiene practices, especially handwashing at critical times. This will be complemented by activities aimed at ensuring sustainability of the WASH services, such as empowering communities in the management of water facilities by establishing and training of institutionalised WASH Committees, putting in place WASH information management systems both at locality and state level to better track progress and address inequities and enhancing capacities of locality and community level WASH practitioners.
Child Protection will be enhanced by ensuring that service providers at the state and local levels in UNICEF targeted areas have strengthened capacities to deliver quality emergency and long-term specialized child-protection services with appropriate referral mechanisms in place. Also, more communities will have strengthened mechanisms to protect children from violence, abuse, and exploitation including female genital mutilation, child marriage and child recruitment,
In order to address the most immediate needs of the at-risk population, while also establishing monitoring and reporting mechanisms on the grave violations of child rights, delivery mechanisms will be mainly through engagement of civil society organizations and local level key government technocrats. Community engagement will be a key component towards ensuring sustainable access to basic social services, particularly through the engagement of community-based child protection networks.

title.narrative: Amendment No.1 to the Agreement on Thematic Support to Child Protection and WASH System Strengthening in Sudan between Sida and United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) (16815)
Decision on UNICEF Thematic Support to Child Protection and WASH System Strengthening in Sudan

description.narrative:
Sida has a longstanding partnership with UNICEF in Sudan, both within the humanitarian and bilateral development portfolios. UNICEF plays a critical role both when it comes to the protection response due to its mandate for Child Protection, and within the food security response through its mandate in WASH and Nutrition. UNICEF is working in all parts of Sudan through its implementing partners, and is a vital actor to ensure pipeline of supplies for treating severe acute malnutrition.
In 2025, Swedish thematic funding supported interventions across multiple high need states in Sudan, ensuring equitable and needsbased geographic coverage.
2025 Child Protection results
During 2025, as part of its child protection efforts, UNICEF strengthened the social service workforce and community based protection mechanisms and expanded access to specialised services across seven states: Kassala, Gedaref, River Nile, Northern, White Nile, Aj Jazirah, and Red Sea.
Specific outputs included:
- 1,435 frontline workers trained and more than 600 social workers retained, ensuring continuity of services despite widespread displacement and system disruption.
- 241 Community-Based Child Protection Networks (CBCPNs) were established and 4,820 members trained, strengthening community-level prevention, identification, and referral mechanisms.
- 3,605 children registered and supported through structured referral pathways.
- Efforts to strengthen child-sensitive justice systems resulted in 33 per cent of children in detention being diverted to alternative measures, while 126 children, including those with disabilities, were transitioned from institutional into family-based care arrangements.
2025 WASH results
To address critical public health risks, UNICEF delivered integrated WASH interventions reaching over 304,000 people across Gedaref, Kassala, and White Nile states that included restoration and expansion of water systems in displacement-affected areas, emergency water provision and cholera response in high-risk locations and community-led sanitation and hygiene interventions.
Specific outputs included:
- 185,733 people reached with access to safe water through rehabilitation of water systems, installation of pumps, and emergency water provision.
- 38,168 people reached with water quality and cholera response interventions, supported by the training of 30 chlorinators and strengthened water safety monitoring systems.
-21,204 people reached with sanitation services and 36,408 people with hygiene promotion activities.
Integrated approaches
The Child Protection and WASH response was characterised by geographic convergence and deliberate integration of services at community level. In targeted areas, populations reached through WASH interventions were simultaneously supported with child protection services, creating a more holistic response to overlapping risks. Community platforms, such as Child Protection Networks and WASH committees, served as joint entry points for outreach, referrals and awarenessraising. ChildFriendly Spaces were equipped with safe water and sanitation, providing protective environments that supported both childrens wellbeing and hygiene needs.
This integrated approach increased efficiency, strengthened community trust and maximised impact by addressing childrens protection and health needs together. Sidas flexible funding enabled rapid, needsbased programming in a fluid environment while reinforcing national and local systems, demonstrating the value of crosssectoral programming in preventing disease, protecting children and promoting resilience.
It is Sida's assessmen that systemlevel investments reduce risks by enabling communities and institutions to withstand shocks and maintain essential services. By reinforcing local capacities and communitybased mechanisms, vulnerabilities and reliance on repeated emergency interventions are reduced while supporting longterm resilience and preparedness. Even in Sudans volatile context, development programming remains both possible and necessary to safeguard gains, support recovery pathways and ensure service delivery as conditions stabilise.
The flexible modality of UNICEF's work bridged the humanitariandevelopment nexus, allowing UNICEF to deliver lifesaving assistance while investing in sustainable, locally owned systems that improve access, quality and accountability for vulnerable children and families.
Sida notes that UNICEF Sudan have reached objectives to support institutional WASH capacity and Child Protection as stated in the 2025 work plan.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
